scope: Actual exported in-process runtime, existing ordered ACP event path and isolated local stdio fixture subprocesses. Node 24.22.1 / pnpm 11.27.1. No native-agent/provider/business call, live ATO, credentials or service mutation.

changes.behavior: Separate opt-in schema-v1 safe sink, independent of assurance and sensitive rich events. Fixed field/status/category allowlist; no arbitrary text/prose/error parsing, raw tools, thoughts, titles, paths, stderr or untrusted _meta authority. Frozen primitive-only records and runtime-salted aliases.

Use the existing per-owner ordered inbound ACP message path before asynchronous SDK update handling. Match the actual dispatched native session and exclude pre-dispatch, wrong-session and post-response reports. No second transport, daemon, event-graph node, notifier or live integration.
changes.evidence: A first implementation observing delayed SDK callbacks dropped valid tool reports when response ingress came first. The final implementation preserves raw ingress ordering and passes both the predecessor two-update case and the new four-update case.

changes.behavior: Correlate the admitted record/caller request, distinct client turn, actual native session/RPC dispatch and turn-scoped tool IDs. The opt-in private assurance receipt supplies a detached observationIdentity alias mapping for caller-owned association of concurrent requests.
changes.evidence: Tests compare the receipt RPC ID with actual subprocess prompt receipts, compare all safe aliases with the terminal observation, and mutate a returned mapping without changing later snapshots. Reused request/tool IDs get distinct turn/tool aliases; runtime salts differ.

changes.behavior: Expose client lifecycle, monotonic sequence/time, elapsed turn/tool observation duration, transport/delivery/turn status, fixed failure categories and separate cancel intent/write/acknowledgement/cleanup. Native tool termination, backend outcome and business validation remain unknown.
changes.evidence: Directed cases cover unsent authority failure, one-effect ambiguous EOF without replay, explicit RPC error, completed transport with finalization failure, ignored cancellation and ordinary empty/completed v1 semantics.

changes.behavior: Count one tracked tool ID once across updates; preserve status on statusless updates. Explicit partial, update_only, untracked, trackingTruncated and ignoredUpdates markers. ACP v1 tool attribution is labeled active_session_window, not native turn proof.
changes.evidence: Four reports retain one ID/count with pending/in_progress/in_progress/failed states. An orphan update remains unknown/update_only; oversized and over-limit IDs remain untracked with a final count of one.

changes.behavior: Bound pending event count/serialized bytes (including in-flight), tracked tool IDs, per-turn total accepted output and each event. Reserve one per-turn output slot for settlement without promising terminal delivery when queue/bytes are full.
changes.evidence: The paced 60-tool/120-update flood emits at most eight events with a configured eight-event budget, reports >=100 dropped events, a sequence gap and tracking truncation at two IDs. A one-byte pending budget emits no records while the turn completes.

changes.behavior: Only one sink call in flight. Disable on throw/rejection or async timeout, count failed/expired in-flight calls once, drop pending records, keep an unresolved slot occupied, never await observation for result or shutdown. Stats retain loss/failure information when terminal events cannot reach the sink.
changes.evidence: Throw/reject/stall/recovery/shutdown/late-rejection cases verify unchanged completed results, <=one concurrent call, bounded bytes, positive drop counters, disabled state, eventual byte release and no repeated timeout/rejection failure count.

limitations: Stage implementation only. Frozen source-loader acceptance remains scheduler/host-owned, with TAP reporter environment required by the unchanged verifier. Full inherited pnpm check/check:docs, coverage, package qualification, independent P2 review, installed-Pi loopback and own-fork branch publication remain later qualification/delivery work. No host pass or total completion is claimed.

ACP v1 has no authenticated turn/request ID on session updates. Same-session delayed activity arriving within a subsequent prompt window cannot be disambiguated; toolCorrelation remains active_session_window and all coverage remains partial. Forged _meta cannot upgrade correlation, trust, permissions or success.

The safe channel sees active-turn client/ACP reports only, not hidden native activity. Replay-suppressed, idle/setup, out-of-window and wrong-session updates are excluded. Tool counts and durations are observed tracking, not exhaustive native totals or execution duration.

Overflow, sink failure, timeout or shutdown can lose a terminal event. Runtime-cumulative dropped/sequence counters and stats must be checked. Locally resolved callbacks do not establish durable external delivery, storage or user notification.

A trusted synchronous CPU-blocking callback cannot be preempted in the same process. Async concurrency/time and retained memory are bounded; external storage and total multi-turn retention remain caller responsibility.

Existing rich event streams, raw wire observers and persisted journals remain sensitive and retain their inherited buffering/retention contracts. The safe channel does not bound or sanitize these separate rich paths.

No remote transport, v2 draft stack, native outcome reader, business validator, new provider, live integration, session migration, scheduler/controller change, original task-history mutation, Git commit/push/release or unsolicited notification was introduced.
